Definition: from G4516; Romæan, i.e. Roman (as noun):--Roman, of Rome.
BiblicalUsage: They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, said Paul at Philippi, and at Jerusalem he asked, is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned? The chief captain feared when he knew Paul was a Roman.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it that Roman citizenship was Paul's shield, and God used the empire's own law to carry His apostle to Rome.
